Materials

Tile trims and angles in aluminium, brass and stainless

Aluminium tile trim is the everyday choice: light, easy to cut and available in the widest range of profiles. Brass tile trim suits warm colour schemes and brushed brass tapware. Stainless steel tile trim is the hard wearing option, and the range includes Grade 304 and marine Grade 316 angles.

Trims are chosen with the tile, so if you are still deciding on the wall, start with our feature wall tiles.

Profiles

Square edge, round edge and L angle

The profile is the shape you see once the tile is in. A tile angle is an L shape that caps a corner. A square edge gives a crisp modern line, and a round edge is softer and kinder to elbows in a shower.

Which trim profile suits which job?

Where it goesProfileExamples on this page

A softer wall edgeHalf round or round edge trimHalf Round Trim, Brass Half Round Trim and Chrome Plated Half Round Trim

Step edgesStair nosingStairnosing and Rubber Stairnosing Insert
Between two floor heightsDiminishing trimAluminium Diminishing Trim
Movement joints in a floorExpansion jointBatex and Mortarloc in aluminium, brass and stainless steel
Shower and balcony edgesWater stop angle, shower bead or balcony trimGeometric Aluminium Angle (Water Stop), Showerstop Bead and Balcony Trim

Profile names are from the BAT Trims range. Our team confirms sizes and finishes when you enquire.

Sizes

Heights from 8 to 12.5mm and 3m lengths

Trim height is matched to the thickness of the tile plus its adhesive bed. Cove trims and corners on this page come in 8, 10 and 12.5 mm, and the Brass Angle in 6, 8, 10, 11 and 12 mm.

Most profiles are sold in 3 m lengths. Some come in 1 m, 1.8 m, 2.5 m and longer lengths, as shown in the product name.

Pricing

Trim prices

The Brass Angle is priced from $39 to $59 for a 3 m length. The BAT Trims profiles show Enquire Now: add what you need to your enquiry and our team confirms the price with you.

The range

BAT Trims range: confirmed on enquiry

The 90 BAT Trims profiles listed here are the ones our supplier offers. Tell us the profile, the size, the finish and the number of lengths, and our team confirms availability before you order.

Choosing

Matching trim height to tile thickness

Take the tile thickness, add a couple of millimetres for the adhesive, and choose the trim height nearest to that. Too low and the tile edge sits proud. Too high and the trim stands above the tile.

Bring a tile to the showroom if you are unsure. The trim is bedded in the right adhesive at the same time as the tile, so buy both together.

Finishes

Finish durability

Finish and wear differ by metal. Stainless steel resists knocks and is the usual choice for steps and commercial floors. Coloured and plated finishes should be protected from grout and cleaning acids while the job is under way.

Ask us for the BAT Trims information on the finish you are choosing.

Collecting

Pick-up

A 3 m length will not fit inside most cars. Bring a ute, roof racks or a van, or ask about delivery with your tiles across Sydney metro.

Trims are part of our trade supplies for tilers.

Supplier

BAT Trims profiles

BAT Trims groups its range into premium trims, project trims, commercial trims and pre-fabricated corner pieces. The corner pieces and end caps on this page save cutting mitres on site.

Tile edging is cut with a fine blade or a mitre saw, and you will find other tools for the tiling job in the tool range.

Aftercare

Cleaning trims after grouting

Wipe grout and adhesive off a trim while they are still wet. Dried grout is abrasive, and scraping it off can mark the finish.

Many trims are supplied with a protective film. Leave it on until the grouting is finished, then peel it away.

Tile trims

Tile trim questions

What size tile trim do I need?

Choose a trim height that matches your tile thickness plus the adhesive bed. For a 9 mm tile, a 10 mm trim is the usual match. Bring a tile in and we will check it against the profile.

Should tile trim match the tile or the tapware?

Either works. Matching the tile makes the trim disappear. Matching the tapware, for example a brass trim with brass taps, turns the tile edge trim into a feature.

What is the difference between square and round edge trim?

A square edge trim finishes the corner with a flat, sharp line. A round edge trim has a curved face, which is softer to the touch and suits traditional bathrooms.

How much is tile trim?

The Brass Angle is priced from $39 to $59 a length. Other tile trims on this page are priced on enquiry, and our team confirms the price for the profile and size you need.

How long is a length of tile trim?

Most tile trims on this page come in 3 m lengths. Some profiles are sold in 1 m, 1.8 m or 2.5 m lengths, as shown in the product name.

Do you sell brass and stainless steel tile trim?

Yes. The range includes Brass Angle, Chrome Plated Brass Angle, and Stainless Steel Angle in Grade 304 and marine Grade 316, along with expansion joints in brass and stainless steel.
